issues.description: Close message string is {"type": "Close"} but Deepgram contract requires {"type": "CloseStream"}.
issues.detail: The PR description and Deepgram's Speak socket docs specify CloseStream as the control message. The code sends Close, which the server likely will not recognize, defeating the entire fix. This is the literal bug the PR claims to resolve, just renamed. Verify against the spec and correct the literal before merge.

issues.description: Single ws.receive() with 1s timeout does not actually drain remaining audio frames.
issues.detail: The stated postcondition is that all remaining audio is processed before close, but one receive() consumes at most one frame. There is no loop, no termination condition tied to a terminal message, and no invariant relating frames received to frames expected. Either loop until CLOSED/deadline or drop the pretense of draining.

issues.description: Bare except Exception swallows cancellation and real programming errors.
issues.detail: The catch-all logs every failure as a warning, hiding ConnectionResetError, aiohttp-specific errors, and asyncio.CancelledError alike. Enumerate the admissible failures (connection-reset, websocket errors) and let unexpected exceptions and cancellation propagate. A blanket except is a smuggled goto into finally that masks bugs.

issues.description: Deepgram control-message constants are duplicated/misplaced instead of shared.
issues.detail: STT already defines a CloseStream control message; TTS now declares its own as class attributes. The Deepgram wire protocol is one ADT — centralize _FLUSH_MSG/_CLOSE_MSG in a shared protocol module (or at least module scope) so STT and TTS cannot drift, and so the constants reflect that they are not part of instance state.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the patch has the right shape — send a control message, briefly wait, then close — but two substantive problems block confidence. First, the close payload is {"type": "Close"} while the PR description and Deepgram docs require {"type": "CloseStream"}; if the server ignores the wrong type, the fix does not fix the bug. Second, a single receive() with a 1s timeout does not satisfy the implied "drain remaining audio" postcondition. Secondary cleanups: narrow the bare except, and centralize the Deepgram control-message constants so STT and TTS share one source of truth. Verify the wire format against the Speak socket spec before merge.
